title.narrative: CO- Oxfam’s Food and Economic Security

description.narrative:
Somalia remains one of the world’s 18 hunger hotspots, with food insecurity driven by recurrent droughts, floods, conflict, and economic volatility. Over the past five years, an average of 3.8 million people; about 22 percent of the population have facedIPC Phase3 or worse conditions. The October–December 2025 projection shows that more than two-thirds of the country’s 90 districts have at least one population group (rural, urban, or IDP) in IPC3+, while 21 districts have pockets of IPC 4 Emergency. Humanitarian ResponsePlan of Food Security and Livelihoods Cluster partners identified 4.5 million people in need. Of these 2.5 million people are prioritized to target with required funding of 515 million USD. As of November, only 1.3 million people are reached and 77.8 million USD – only 15 precent of required funding is secured. Food Security plans of HNRP were funded 66 percent in 2024 but only 11 percent bySeptember 2025. UN World Food Program (WFP) issued official communication in October 2025 to discontinue its cash-based assistance to 800,000 people every month starting from 1 November due to unavailability of funds. Among Oxfam’s 26 targeted districts, 9 include population groups reaching IPC4, and over 20 have populations in IPC3+, with an average 30 to 35 percent of population in crisis or worse compared to 23 percent nationally.Oxfam’s current food security response has achieved 40% of plan due to available funding.
Oxfam’s Food and Economic Security Response Plan:
Sector Objective: Toenable 138,115 food-insecure (IPC3+) people (Women: 28,049; Girls: 41,312; Men: 25,165; Boys: 43,590; Persons with disabilities: 6,906) in 26 priority districts to meet their food and basic needs through cash, vouchers, multipurpose cash assistance, and livelihoods support, with particular attention to IDPs, women, children, persons with disabilities, and other vulnerable groups.
Target locations: Belet Weyne district in Hiran region and Baardheere district in Gedo region of Somalia.
1. Targeted 400 (approx. 2,400 people) most vulnerable internally displaced and host households (primarily 2 vulnerability criteria to priorities: female headed household with no earning male member and poor households headed/member by person with disability), have improved immediate access to food through vouchers, enabling them to meet their basic food needs, reduce food gaps, and minimize the use of negative coping strategies. Voucher assistance to adopt 55 USD per month per household transfer value recommended by Food Security Cluster. Total 6 months of assistance is proposed for each household. 2. Targeted 1,750 households enhance their food security and resilience through the timely use of emergency agricultural inputs, leading to increased local food productionfrom short-cycle, early maturing crops, improved dietary diversity, and reduced dependence on external food assistance. Voucher value of 45 USD per household is adopted based Food Security and Livelihoods Cluster recommendation.
Total Beneficiaries: approx.. 12,900 people.

participating-org.narrative: In 2004 Oxfam Novib set up a Liaison Office in Nairobi, Kenya in order to support the Strengthening Somali Civil Society Program, at the request of the EU. This request was based on Oxfam Novib's work in Somalia to date, but intended to be more widely directed atthe entire civil society sector and the specific context in which it is operating in a post-conflict country. The program started with consulting local organisations in Somalia and Somaliland to get a complete picture of the sectors and regions where they are active, the challenges they face and the relationship between civil society, local political structures and the private sector. A program was then developed to strengthen the institutional development of Oxfam Novib's partners and those of other Oxfams, as well as a range of new NGOs. In the first year local consultants were trained in Somalia. They were then seconded to civil society organisations to build their capacity in financial and organisational management. Furthermore, workshops were organised on specific themes suchas human rights and the role of civil society in the Somali context. The Liaison Office is now going to support the expansion of the program, focussing on strengthening both organisation and project management, while facilitating more training in the fields of civic education, governance, human rights and women's rights, HIV and AIDS and child protection. Over the years, the Somalia Country Office has expanded its intervention on short term humanitarian response as well as development development interventions. In 2015/2016, a decision was reached to move the Country Programme operation, which was largely in Nairobi, from Nairobi to Hargeisa. The country office has a small office in Nairobi , Kenya and large operations office in Hargeisa, Somaliland.
